content.value: The Vitals feature allow the user to retrieve patient vitals measurements, record vitals to the patient's flowsheet. Patient vitals elements are configured by the practice. All patient vitals are returned regardless of source, but the adding of vitals here is only when it's outside the context of an encounter. If you wish to add vitals to an encounter, please use the POST /chart/encounter/{encounterid}/vitals endpoint instead. Please note that if you do add vitals using this endpoint, you are responsible for notifying the provider or practice about any clinically relevant data or results. See the GET /chart/configuration/vitals endpoint for the list of available vitals this practice accepts. The Vitals Reference feature allows the user to retrieve the list of vitals configured for a practice. We do not currently have support for non-vital ambulatory chart measurements. For example, non-vitals such as blood glucose, last menstrual period, etc. will not be returned in the vitals endpoints.

API users can add and update vitals that occur outside an encounter (i.e., an encounterid is not required). The only vitals allowed to be posted/updated through these endpoints are device-generated vitals. Device-generated vitals are measurements taken by a device (e.g., blood pressure cuff, pulse oximeter) connected to the partner’s application. The device-generated vitals simulate a practice member entering vitals measurements directly into a patient’s flowsheet.

The user’s application must be the primary source of the vitals information. API users are responsible for contacting the patient’s care manager or physician if the vitals are outside a set threshold. The vitals added through the endpoint are a back-up of the measurements presented in the partner’s application.
Retrieve a patient’s vitals via: GET /chart/{patientid}/vitals
This returns a list of vitals tied to the patient, and for each vital, a list of readings (in different subsections). By default, only the attributes that have readings for the patient are returned.
However, you can get the complete list via: GET /chart/{patientid}/vitals&showemptyvitals=true
The vitals value in the POST API is a complex url-encoded JSON structure. It’s an array of arrays. Each subarray contains a group of related readings.
All of the vital attributes must have the readingtaken date.
You may not post vitals with different readingtaken dates in the same POST.
If no readingtaken date is given, the date defaults to the current day.
Multiple vitals measurements can be posted for the same date.
The list of readings returned by the GET contains a vitalid value. This uniquely identifies that particular reading.
You can use the vitalid to update the value of that particular reading via: PUT/chart/{patientid}/vitals/{vitalid}

primaryEndpoints.endpointDescription: Retrieves the vital signs data obtained from the patient during the clinical encounter

inputParameters.name: practiceid
inputParameters.description: practiceid

inputParameters.name: patientid
inputParameters.description: patientid

inputParameters.name: departmentid
inputParameters.description: The department from which to retrieve the patient's chart.

inputParameters.name: encounterid
inputParameters.description: The encounter vitals are associated with.

inputParameters.name: enddate
inputParameters.description: For date filterable items, exclude data after this datetime. Format is MM/DD/YYYY HH24:MM:SS.

inputParameters.name: xmloutput
inputParameters.description: If set to true, use XML (not JSON) as output.  Not needed if an Accept header with application/xml header is included in the request. If set to false, it will return the CCDA format (XML) wrapped in a JSON response.

inputParameters.name: startdate
inputParameters.description: For date filterable items, exclude data before this datetime. Format is MM/DD/YYYY HH24:MM:SS.

inputParameters.name: format
inputParameters.description: Document type.

inputParameters.name: limit
inputParameters.description: Number of entries to return (default 1000, max 10000)Please note that this endpoint has a different default and max than normal.

inputParameters.name: offset
inputParameters.description: Starting point of entries; 0-indexed

inputParameters.name: THIRDPARTYUSERNAME
inputParameters.description: User name of the patient in the third party application.

inputParameters.name: PATIENTFACINGCALL
inputParameters.description: When 'true' is passed we will collect relevant data and store in our database.

abbreviation.description: Short human-readable string for this vital group. E.g., Ht.

key.description: Key for this vital group. E.g., HEIGHT.

ordering.description: Configured order for this vital group

readings.description: List of vital attribute readings. One entry per attribute (so the temperature and where the temperature was taken are two different readings, tied together by the readingid

clinicalelementid.description: Key used to identify this particular vital attribute

createdby.description: The athenaNet username of the person who entered the vital.

createddate.description: The date this vital was entered into the chart. Returned in mm/dd/yyyy hh24:mi:ss format.

isgraphable.description: Flag indicating if this vital is graphable.

lastmodifiedby.description: The athenaNet username of the user that last modified the reading.

lastmodifieddate.description: The date this vital was last modified. Returned in mm/dd/yyyy hh24:mi:ss format.

high.description: The highest value the y value could be.

low.description: The lowest value that y could be.

prefix.description: Indicator of less than or greater. Possible values: (>,<)

readingid.description: Numeric key used to tie related and distinguish separate readings. So the diastolic and systolic blood pressure should have the same readingid.

readingtaken.description: Date that the reading was taken.

unit.description: Unit that describes this vital's value.

value.description: The value of this reading. NOTE: for numeric values, the units are always in the 'native' units per the configuration.

vitalid.description: Unique ID for this vital attribute reading. Used to update/delete this reading.

primaryEndpoints.endpointDescription: Records the source of the data and vitals measurements of the patient.

inputParameters.name: practiceid
inputParameters.description: practiceid

inputParameters.name: patientid
inputParameters.description: patientid

inputParameters.name: Content-Type
inputParameters.description: Content type of the payload

source.description: Where this vital was collected. For now only device generated is allowed. Later, we will use this to differentiate between patient reported, device generated, and practice collected vitals outside of an encounter.

vitals.description: This is an array of arrays in JSON. Each subarray contains a group of related readings, like systolic and diastolic blood pressure. They will be assigned the same readingID.

departmentid.description: The ID of the department of the patient. Used to choose the correct patient chart.

returnvitalids.description: Return the IDs of the newly added vitals, mapped to their vital attribute IDs, in addition to any regular success/error messages.

PATIENTFACINGCALL.description: When 'true' is passed we will collect relevant data and store in our database.

THIRDPARTYUSERNAME.description: User name of the patient in the third party application.

errormessage.description: If the operation failed, this will contain any error messages.

success.description: Whether the operation was successful or not.

vitalids.description: The IDs and clinical element IDs of the newly added vital readings.

clinicalelementid.description: The clinical element ID of a newly added vital reading.

vitalid.description: The ID of a newly added vital reading.
